summary: This is an Explanation of Benefits from Lone Star Benefit Solutions, dated September 5, 2026. It covers care from Gulf Coast Emergency Physicians, PLLC on August 14, 2026: a level 4 emergency department visit (CPT 99284) and a CT scan of the abdomen (CPT 74176). The provider billed $4,800. Your plan paid $1,321.60 and says you may owe $3,478.40. The reason given is code N-661: "Provider is not in your plan's network. Services from a non-participating provider are paid at the out-of-network rate." Code PR-45 also appears. The document says you may file an appeal in writing within 180 days of the date of this statement. It does not state whether any surprise-billing protection was applied.

terms.definition: A statement from your plan showing what a provider charged, what the plan paid, and what you may owe; it is not a bill.
Providers without a contract with your plan, where your costs are usually higher unless a surprise-billing protection applies.
Any doctor, hospital, lab, or clinic that gives you care.
A formal request asking your plan to change its decision.
When an out-of-network provider bills you for the difference between what they charged and what your plan paid; the No Surprises Act bans this in emergencies and at in-network facilities.
A standard number used to identify a specific medical service on a bill.
